title: GitLab Bets on AI Agents, Cuts Staff and Country Footprint
excerpt: CEO Bill Staples launches 'GitLab Act 2' — flattening management, shrinking global presence, and betting savings on the agentic era.
body:
GitLab fired the starting gun on a sweeping corporate overhaul on May 11, 2026, announcing a global workforce reduction and operational redesign it calls 'GitLab Act 2' — a deliberate pivot toward what CEO Bill Staples describes as the 'agentic era' of AI-driven software development.

**What GitLab announced:**
The company launched a restructuring and global workforce reduction plan to realign its operations for the agentic era of AI. GitLab plans to cut its country footprint by about 30%, flatten management layers, reorganize R&D into roughly 60 smaller, more autonomous teams, and use AI agents to automate internal processes. Staples has not yet disclosed how many roles the process will eliminate — that number lands on June 2, when the company reports quarterly earnings.

**Why now — and what it signals:**
For fiscal year 2026, which ended in January, GitLab reported $955 million in revenue, up 26% year over year, with annual recurring revenue surpassing one billion dollars. But the deceleration from 26% to a projected 16% growth rate is the real context for this restructuring. Staples, who frames the move as a strategic reinvestment rather than a cost cut, said the company will channel savings back into AI infrastructure. The stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading.

**What comes next:**
On May 11, 2026, GitLab announced its intention to execute a reduction in force intended to help position the company for long-term success by realigning its operating structure. GitLab will share the next wave of its innovation roadmap at GitLab Transcend on June 10, 2026. Watch the June 2 earnings call — that is when the true human cost of this transformation becomes clear.
